why:
phase-456 W9 — an UPSTREAM name on an ours-only type, which is why it needs a row of its own rather than inheriting `cpp:ClientHandle`'s. The substantive verdict against `rclcpp::Client::async_send_request` — upstream returns a `std::shared_future` keyed by the sequence number, ours returns a `Result` and the reply reaches the handler bound at registration — stays at `cpp:Client::async_send_request`, which is where the comparison lives. This row records that the verb is ALSO on the handle, and why it can be: it needs `{executor, handle_id}` and nothing else, so the two words a keep-alive would have carried are already the whole send road.

THIS IS THE ROW THAT MAKES THE HANDLE FAMILY NON-UNIFORM, deliberately. `cpp:SubscriptionHandle` and `cpp:ServiceHandle` carry no verb because the census measured none; this one does because the census measured one. Held by the two-directional reachability assertions in `tests/compile/ros2_api_adoption.cpp` — the handle HAS it, `ServiceHandle` does NOT — because a silent loss of the method would leave every other assertion about this type green.
